svg.title: Conv2D speech embedding: four times shorter in time
svg.desc: The normalised filterbank, 1 channel by 1761 frames by 80 bins, passes through two 3 by 3 convolutions with stride 2 in time and 1 in frequency, each followed by GELU: 256 by 880 by 78, then 256 by 439 by 76. Channels and remaining frequency positions are flattened to 19456 values per step and projected to 256, giving 439 vectors. Each output step moves 4 input frames and sees a window of 7 frames.
svg.text: Time: 1,761 → 880 → 439 frames (no padding, so each conv gives ⌊(T − 3) / 2⌋ + 1). Frequency: 80 → 78 → 76, then folded into the channels.
Self-attention cost grows with T², so a 4× shorter sequence makes every encoder layer about 16× cheaper.
RECEPTIVE FIELD · one encoder step = 4 frames apart, 7 frames wide
frames 1148–1170 of the normalised utterance (all 80 bins)
Each bracket is the span of input frames one output vector depends on: conv 1 sees 3 frames, conv 2 sees 3 conv-1 outputs that are 2 frames apart, so 3 + 2·2 = 7 frames.
